parts.description: A spatula knife featuring a flat stainless steel blade with an offset angle, attached to a wooden handle secured by three metal rivets.
parts.reasoning: Based on the provided telemetry, the object measures approximately 0.25m in length with a voxel volume of 3.77e-5 m³. The material composition is a mix of stainless steel (the blade and full tang) and wood (the handle scales). By blending the typical densities of steel (~8000 kg/m³) and wood (~700 kg/m³), an average density of 4000 kg/m³ is applied, yielding a highly realistic total mass of 0.15 kg. Convex decomposition is chosen for the collision geometry to accurately capture the concave bend where the offset blade meets the handle, which a simple convex hull would incorrectly bridge. Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is enabled because the thin metal blade is highly susceptible to tunneling through surfaces during dynamic or robotic interactions. Contact offsets are reduced to 0.001m to maintain tight contact constraints around the thin blade edges. Friction and restitution values reflect a blend of smooth metallic and polished wooden surfaces.
